requirements.requirement: Three-member Galera cluster established across node1/node2/node3, holding application data
requirements.summary: After bootstrap+join, cmd-1878a63d1de5497e shows wsrep_cluster_size=3, status Primary, state Synced, with incoming addresses for all three nodes. appdb.orders was created and 3 rows inserted on node1 (cmd-15a01f4aa0fd4d8f, later a 4th row via cmd-9448d2b48966424f) and independently confirmed present via SELECT on node2 (cmd-51b89be833eb4e8c) and node3 (cmd-dab8bf5aa99c4156).

requirements.requirement: Cluster brought down completely for a maintenance window
requirements.summary: node2 stopped (cmd-609bd1a1d4ae46db, is-active -> inactive), node3 stopped (cmd-411775ea183f4213, inactive), node1 stopped last (cmd-593ed91256834b08, inactive) with grastate.dat showing safe_to_bootstrap:1 for a clean shutdown record. All three were confirmed inactive in sequence, directly showing a full-cluster down state.

requirements.requirement: Cluster brought back after maintenance with every committed write present and all three members serving
requirements.summary: node1 rebootstrapped via galera_new_cluster (cmd-e8d0521337b74fc7) and immediately showed all 4 committed rows. node2 (cmd-a94accf73a0642b6) and node3 (cmd-bd9ca2581f41440c) rejoined and started successfully. Post-recovery checks (cmd-f60e959387cb46ea, cmd-b776074d00734afb, cmd-90c3a5352e1141a8) confirm cluster_size=3, Primary, Synced, and identical 4-row dataset on every node; final cross-check (cmd-067a2c141b444181) reconfirms size 3, all incoming addresses, and correct row count/sum.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide sequential node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes (baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state)
requirements.summary: Each node shows a pre-restart boot_id baseline, an async systemctl reboot acknowledgement, connection loss during the transition, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and confirmed mariadb active with cluster_size=3/Synced (Primary for node1 and node3) and the full 4-row dataset intact. This is cross-checked by the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which independently show matching boot_id changes for all three nodes (fb2aa416->758116b3, 45c22b1f->e1ae058d, bccb87ac->d21d7a69) and healthy listening sockets (3306/4567) post-restart with no failed services.

overall_summary: The executor deployed a working 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster from scratch, loaded application data, performed a full simultaneous shutdown of all three nodes for a maintenance window, and brought the cluster back with all four committed rows present and all three members rejoined and Synced. It additionally executed the mandatory per-node reboot protocol on all three nodes with clear before/after boot-identity evidence, disconnection during reboot, and confirmed post-reboot cluster/data recovery, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity and listening-socket snapshots. All four material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. Hygiene is good but not perfect: a debugging package (strace) and various /tmp log artifacts from install/reboot/troubleshooting were left behind on all nodes, and root/SST secret files remain on disk in plaintext form (though permission-restricted).
limitations: Evidence for the maintenance shutdown relies on sequential systemctl stop calls with only the final node's is-active check confirming inactivity at that moment; there is no single simultaneous cluster-wide snapshot proving all three were down at the exact same instant, though the ordering and grastate.dat capture support a genuine full shutdown.
Root and SST auth passwords are stored as plaintext files (mode 600) on all three nodes and were not removed after use; this is standard for lab automation but represents residual sensitive material.

Minor executor-created residue (extra installed strace package, assorted /tmp log files) remains on all three nodes per the after_executor snapshot; this does not affect cluster functionality but is a hygiene deduction.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing troubleshooting was purposeful and properly resolved: the custom SELinux policy module built via audit2allow/semodule -i (cmd-c590b47a3f7d4740) was explicitly removed (semodule -r, cmd-e81381aeb5a246e1) and replaced with the supported daemons_enable_cluster_mode boolean, and the corrupted /var/lib/mysql on node2 after a failed SST was deliberately wiped and reinitialized (cmd-1449dcc85bab45df, cmd-1b0a6bc53c104558) as a corrective action rather than residue. However, several low-risk items were left behind and are unnecessary mutations relative to the task: the strace package was installed for debugging (cmd-b2b7310c66f143f4) and never removed; numerous /tmp log/pid files from install and reboot attempts (install.log, gnc.log, gnc2.log, mariadbd.log, strace.log, reboot.log, start.log, etc.) remain on all three nodes per the after_executor temporary-files diff; and plaintext secret files (/root/.sst_pass, /root/.mysql_root_pass) remain readable on disk (chmod 600) rather than being cleaned up after cluster-wide propagation. None of these are broad, destructive, or security-weakening beyond minor residue, so hygiene is scored as good but not perfect.
